body.statement: Using \(def:direct-calibration-handle\), determine the robust perturbation blocks, bounded-influence score, polynomial constants, and score-inversion critical value for which \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) is measurable from \(\mathcal D_n\) and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{|\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\widehat T_{\mathrm L}|>\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\}\le\alpha/4\) together with \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat R_{\mathrm L}]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every valid \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\), the coefficient recurrence, factorial recurrence, outward score evaluation, and bisection in \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) must return a certified approximation to \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) with absolute error at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/4\). The tail certificate must concern the selected marked-factorial statistic itself rather than a Markov conversion of its mean squared error, a cellwise union bound, or a generic median-of-means wrapper.
body.justification: This remains the central inference obstruction: a direct tail event must be proved for the selected marked-factorial statistic itself and must also handle pilot-dependent centering.
body.gap: The directed symmetric half-log score is not monotone and can have multiple roots, so Catoni2012 does not supply the requested unique-root or numerical-inversion theorem. A retained-range proof or corrected monotone score is necessary before the factorial MGF calculation can close.
body.consumer: A deployable rare-cell coverage certificate for saturated adjustment remains the intended consumer.

obligation.what_is_open: An explicit data-measurable rare-cell score interval with a directly proved tail event, sharp expected radius, and certified root inversion for the pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic.
obligation.obstruction: The stipulated transform \(\psi(x)=\tfrac12\log\{(1+x+x^2/2)/(1-x+x^2/2)\}\) satisfies \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\), so it is not globally monotone. For odd \(B\ge3\), block values consisting of \(B-1\) zeros and one sufficiently remote value make the summed score change sign at least three times; thus the requested unique root, monotone score inversion, and a uniform positive slope modulus do not follow. In addition, conditioning on the common pilot controls fluctuations about a pilot-dependent block mean, not automatically about the unconditional expectation appearing in the target. The frozen bank supplies a factorial covariance calculation but neither a pilot-fluctuation score nor a retained range that repairs these two gaps.
obligation.attempted: I instantiated the directed constants \(K=\lfloor\alpha_0\log(em)\rfloor\), pilot threshold \(256\log(em)\), and mass scale \(4096\log(em)/m\), and set up the ordered-index overlap enumeration for a conditional block variance calculation. Before using an MGF inequality, I differentiated the exact proposed score and tested its root equation. That audit fails at uniqueness and monotone inversion, independently of any forbidden MSE-to-Chebyshev conversion, so asserting the requested block-tail certificate would skip an earlier necessary step.
obligation.partial_result:
The established node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the bias
\(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  The stipulated score, however, does not yet
turn this fact into the requested observable tail radius.  Indeed, for
\[
 \psi(x)=\frac12\log\frac{1+x+x^2/2}{1-x+x^2/2}
\]
one has
\[
 \psi'(x)=\frac{2(2-x^2)}{x^4+4}.
\]
Thus the score is increasing only on \((-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\) and is decreasing
outside that interval.  More concretely, for any odd block count \(B\ge3\)
and any \(\lambda>0\), consider algebraic block outputs
\(Z_1=\cdots=Z_{B-1}=0\) and \(Z_B=R/\lambda\).  The proposed score is
\[
 S_R(t)=-(B-1)\psi(\lambda t)+\psi(R-\lambda t).
\]
For sufficiently large \(R\), continuity and
\(\psi(x)\downarrow0\) as \(x\to\infty\) give
\[
 S_R(0)>0,\quad S_R(\sqrt2/\lambda)<0,\quad
 S_R((R-\sqrt2)/\lambda)>0,\quad S_R(R/\lambda)<0.
\]
Hence the zero equation has at least three roots.  A retained-range argument
could still repair uniqueness, but no such range or a positive slope modulus
is presently part of the construction, and the unbounded outcome model does
not supply one automatically.
